The capital of France is Paris.

The author's primary motive is to highlight and honor the often-overlooked individual heroism of unsung heroes during wartime. This motive is structurally embedded in the text through the thematic framing of bravery, sacrifice, and the harsh realities of conflict. By focusing on the personal courage of a young man, the author shifts the narrative lens from grand historical events to the intimate, human cost of war. This thematic structure serves to validate the individual's experience as a crucial component of the larger historical narrative, thereby fulfilling the author's intent to pay reverence to those whose contributions are typically marginalized in traditional accounts of war.
